decision: Reject the premise of AMA-2520 as written
why: The ticket (which I wrote) claimed ancestor identifiers always overwrite descendants. A live dump of the workout detail screen shows af_workout_detail_screen coexisting with af_workout_detail_hero, af_workout_detail_title and af_workout_detail_blocks.
result: VERIFIED false. Shadowing is conditional, not universal.

decision: Identify the real mechanism as a missing children:.contain
why: af_workout_detail_hero survives an ancestor identifier and declares .accessibilityElement(children: .contain). af_tabbar and af_detail_actions shadow and do not.

decision: Test children:.contain on af_detail_actions before designing the sweep
why: Riskiest unknown first. The whole sweep's fix shape depends on this being the mechanism.
evidence: Before: af_detail_pin/collect/towatch/share absent from dump. After: all four present alongside af_detail_actions.
result: VERIFIED. This is the canonical fix.

decision: Replace the af_tabbar marker overlay shipped in #638 with children:.contain
why: The marker (1x1 Text) works but is a hack. The sweep should establish one pattern, not propagate mine.
Referenced only by itself. Not a member of the app target. An orphan file whose name promises a contract it does not provide.
evidence: git grep -ln UITestAccessibility returns only the file itself

decision: Delete AFTabBar and AFTabBarButton from ContentView.swift
why: Referenced only from two #Preview blocks. Not what renders. Cost two full rebuilds during AMA-2514 before I found DDFloatingTabBar.
evidence: git grep AFTabBar shows only self-references plus previews

decision: Build a static detector rather than review 959 call sites by hand
why: 959 accessibilityIdentifier call sites across 181 files. Hand review is not checkable by a reviewer.

decision: Do NOT gate CI on the detector
why: Source position cannot prove an ancestor relationship; the heuristic yields false positives. A gate that cries wolf gets ignored, which is the failure mode this epic is about.
evidence: 182 candidates across 680 files, several verified false
result: DECIDED: triage tool, not a gate.

decision: Do NOT blanket-apply children:.contain to all candidates
why: The modifier changes VoiceOver grouping. Applying it to 182 sites unverified would trade a test bug for an accessibility regression.

decision: Rank candidates by whether automation depends on the hidden identifier
why: Gives a falsifiable impact filter instead of a raw count. 205 identifiers are referenced by flows and XCUITests.
evidence: 27 of 182 candidates hide an automation-referenced identifier
result: Narrows the sweep to a tractable, evidence-backed set.

why: The detector's first finding for that file. The Start button rendered on screen but reported resource-id af_workout_detail_screen, so the screen identifier was swallowing the whole subtree.
evidence: Before: af_workout_detail_start absent, flow failed there. After: tap COMPLETED and af_start_sheet visible.
result: VERIFIED. Unblocks the AMA-2514 flows past their last identifier failure.

decision: Confirm the af_tabbar swap from marker to children:.contain
why: #638 shipped a 1x1 Text marker. The sweep should leave one pattern behind, not two.
evidence: ama-2292: af_tabbar, today_tab, library_tab, profile_tab all assert visible; both id taps COMPLETED.

decision: Do NOT rewrite the "Tap to pair CIQ" assertion to match current copy
why: The Garmin row now reads "Downloads via the AmakaFlow widget" after the AMA-2371 redesign. Editing the assertion to match whatever the app says turns a regression check into a tautology, and the correct copy is a product decision.
evidence: live hierarchy of the start sheet
result: DECIDED: report as flow copy rot, do not silently fix.

decision: Ship the detector as triage, not a CI gate
why: Three true positives found (af_tabbar, af_detail_actions, af_workout_detail_screen) but source position cannot prove an ancestor relationship, so false positives are inherent.
result: DECIDED. --impact ranks by whether a flow or XCUITest names the hidden identifier.
